First, we substitute $u=4t+3.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=4\,⟹\,\text{d}u=4\text{d}t.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $t\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=4t+3$ is as follows:

| $t$ | $-\infty $ | $-1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\infty $ | $-1$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{10}{(4t+3)^{4}}\,\text{d}t={\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{5}{2{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-1}\frac{5}{2{u}^{4}}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-1}{u}^{-4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{3}{u}^{-3}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{5}{6}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{u}^{3}}]}_{a}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{5}{6}\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-1)^{3}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}] \\  & =-\frac{5}{6}\cdot (-1-0) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
